text.p: Dismantling South African currency exchange controls will pave the way for "phenomenal" growth for the South Africa Futures Exchange (SAFFEX), the head of the exchange said Friday.
Removal of the controls would be a "mini-big-bang, I suppose, for our economy," Stuart Rees, SAFFEX chief executive, said in an interview at the Futures Industry Association meeting.
In this new environment, he said, a rand currency futures contract at the SAFFEX was likely.

"The lifting of exchange control certainly will be mean that our market in the short term is going to enjoy phenomenal growth," Rees siad. "The impact of the gradual lifting of exchange control will just be phenomenal for the futures market in South Africa."
South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel took a significant step on Wednesday toward dismantling foreign exchange controls in a disciplined budget that included a tight rein on spending.
Manuel's budget speech announced measures to relax remaining exchange controls on South African nationals and residents.
In 1996, SAFFEX traded 9.3 million contracts, up 26 percent from the previous year, Rees said. January and February 1997 volume increased 58 percent over the same period last year, he said.
